story:
Maya stepped off the bus and held the strap of her backpack a little tighter. It was her first day at a new school, and everything felt unfamiliar. The building looked bigger than her old school, and the hallways were full of students she had never met.

In homeroom, the teacher smiled and asked Maya to introduce herself. Maya's heart beat quickly. She gave a small smile and said, "Hi, I'm Maya." Then she looked down at her shoes.

After class, a girl with a kind smile walked up to her. "Hi, I'm Leah," she said. "I'm new here too. Want to sit together at lunch?" Maya felt a little more relaxed. Maybe this new school wouldn't be so scary after all.

Ana set her lemon cake on the table at the school bake sale. She felt nervous as people started to arrive. When the first customer walked past without looking, Ana bit her lip. Her friend Ben gave her a nudge and said, "Don't worry, it will sell like hot cakes." By noon, every slice was gone. Ana grinned all the way home.
Jonah read the letter from the school twice. Then he folded it very small and pushed it to the bottom of his drawer. He told his mum that everything was fine. He did not come down for dinner.

Omar had worked on his volcano for three weeks. On the morning of the science fair, he carried it carefully into the gym. His older sister walked beside him with the poster. At the door, she patted his shoulder and said, "Break a leg." Omar nodded and went inside.

He set the volcano on his table and poured in the vinegar. Nothing happened. The red liquid sat in the cone and did not bubble at all. "Oh, great," Omar said, frowning at the table.

Then he noticed the baking soda was still in his bag. He added it, and the volcano finally foamed over the sides. A judge wrote something on her clipboard and smiled.

Lena ran to the gym to see the team list. Her name was not on it. She read the list again, slowly, from the top. On the walk home, she kicked a stone all the way to her door.

Priya and Jess met at the park after school. Priya brought a frisbee, and Jess brought a bag of oranges. They found a flat patch of grass near the pond.

Jess threw the frisbee too hard, and it landed in a tree. Priya laughed and climbed up to get it. When she came down, her knee was scraped. Jess gave her a tissue from the bag.

They sat by the pond and shared the oranges. The frisbee stayed on the grass for the rest of the afternoon.

The bus broke down in the rain, and we had to walk the last mile. When we finally arrived, soaked, Nora said, "Well, that was fun."
Sam spilled juice on his homework, then dropped his phone in the sink. "This is my lucky day," he muttered.
Zoe opened the small box. Inside was the thing she had wanted for months. She put it in her pocket.
Mr. Hall read the message on his phone and put it away. Then he started the lesson.
Ivy packed one more thing into her bag before the trip. Then she zipped it shut and left.
